result.target_topic: USG export control licensing requirements for specific products and regions
result.target_summary: Beginning in Q3 FY2023, the USG imposed licensing requirements on exports of A100, H100, and other high-performance AI products to China, Russia, and certain Middle Eastern countries, with new rules effective in Q4 FY2024 covering additional regions like Saudi Arabia and Vietnam. These rules require licenses for shipments of products exceeding specific performance thresholds to these restricted regions or entities linked to Country Group D5.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: These disclosures form a comprehensive view of US government export control risks affecting China and Russia. 2023 D013 and D014 detail the initial license requirements (A100/H100), the requirement to transition operations, and risks of customer rejection of alternatives or license denial. 2024 D009, D010, and D011 expand on this: D009 details the expanded scope of license requirements (including Middle East and newer chips); D010 reports the financial impact (revenue decline) and lack of licenses received; D011 reiterates the risk of license denial and competitive harm from changing rules. The specific shared topic is the regulatory and competitive risk landscape of US export controls on high-performance computing to restricted regions.

previous_disclosures.summary: In Q3 FY2023, the USG announced new license requirements impacting exports of A100, H100, A100X chips and related systems to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Russia, requiring the company to transition R&D and supply/distribution operations out of China.

The company faces risks that customer results and competitive position may be harmed if they reject alternative products like the A800, switch to competitors, develop internal solutions, or if license approvals are delayed or denied.

current_disclosures.summary: Beginning in Q3 FY2023, the USG imposed licensing requirements on exports of A100, H100, and other high-performance AI products to China, Russia, and certain Middle Eastern countries, with new rules effective in Q4 FY2024 covering additional regions like Saudi Arabia and Vietnam. These rules require licenses for shipments of products exceeding specific performance thresholds to these restricted regions or entities linked to Country Group D5.

Sales to China declined from 19% of Data Center revenue in FY2023 to 14% in FY2024, representing a mid-single digit percentage in Q4 FY2024 due to these restrictions. The company has not received licenses for restricted products to China but is shipping alternative solutions in small volumes and expects China revenue to remain in a similar low range in Q1 FY2025.

The company may seek licenses for customers requiring restricted products but has no assurance of approval or timely processing. Competitive position may be harmed by current or future USG export control changes, which could prevent selling inventory or developing replacement products, potentially excluding the company from China and other impacted markets like the Middle East.
